Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing generalized fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests; to understand the underlying cause, I need to ask you a few questions.

To start, have you noticed any jaundice, such as yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, or any changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, age, and multiple sexual partners, could you please list any specific medications you have been taking recently, especially immunosuppressants like azathioprine or methotrexate? Additionally, have you had any recent changes in your bowel habits or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC).

The confirmation of scleral icterus and multiple scratch marks confirms significant cholestasis and pruritus. Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the classic triad of fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice, this presentation is highly suggestive of an autoimmune liver disease associated with autoimmune conditions. I am ready to finalize the diagnosis based on these clinical findings.
